source_pins.finding: A positive maxsize bounds Queue, but await put() blocks while full; put_nowait() raises QueueFull. PriorityQueue changes dequeue order but does not supply stale-work conflation semantics.
Queue limits bound buffers/bytes/time; default full behavior blocks the producer, while leaky mode can drop new or old buffers explicitly. Current-level metrics are observable.
Slow consumers can accumulate memory; max-buffers/max-time/max-bytes bound the queue, leaky-type chooses drop policy, and blocking the streaming thread can harm realtime performance.

CONFLATE demonstrates a latest-value mailbox that keeps only the last queued message, but has an explicit caveat that inbound memory may still grow unless recv/event processing occurs; it is therefore a semantic reference, not a zero-growth guarantee or required dependency.

CapacityLimiter supports zero total tokens in current 4.14.x and dynamic capacity, but recent 4.14.2 fixes include an asyncio token over-grant race. A concurrency limiter is a useful reference, but adding AnyIO only for WP710 would need version pinning and invariant tests.

f2_observation.current_mechanism: deterministic bounded queue; priority/deadline/work-cost rank; coalescing; drop accounting; dispatch-time permission revalidation; 0..4 selected workers; control reserve; pressure shedding; first-pass source diversity
f2_observation.alignment: The implementation already structurally distills the strongest external mechanisms without requiring asyncio/GStreamer/ZeroMQ/AnyIO as scheduler dependencies.
f2_observation.falsifier_candidate: _coalesce_key() does not bind required_freshness_ns, expires_monotonic_ns, cycle_id or permission_snapshot_sha256, while _preferred_coalesced() prefers later expiry after generation/priority. Two superficially similar intents can therefore be treated as equivalent even when one carries a stricter freshness/deadline/authority request. Keeping the looser/later request can discard the stricter sensing obligation before dispatch.
f2_observation.evidence_boundary: This is source-level semantic analysis only. No executable WP710 failure has been reproduced in this Trigger-6 stage.

result: Do not import a heavyweight scheduler. Preserve the native bounded scheduler, but treat coalescing equivalence as the highest-value next discriminator: latest-wins is safe only when the retained request semantically dominates the discarded request or when a merged request preserves the strictest freshness/deadline/permission constraints.
counterhypothesis: If required_freshness_ns is downstream-only metadata and every later-generation intent is guaranteed by a stronger upstream contract to subsume all earlier constraints, the current coalescing rule may be safe; that dominance guarantee is not established by the observed source and must be executable or contract-bound before relying on it.
next_discriminator: Construct an E2 architecture map and then an executable unit falsifier with two same-key intents whose freshness/deadline constraints differ. The test should fail if enqueue coalescing silently drops the stricter still-valid obligation in favor of a looser later-expiry intent.
